reviews.author: Lily Tatusko
reviews.text: There’s some true disparity between the tent sites. We stayed at B9 and it was awesome!! There was even a little secret forest spot you could tuck a tent into. The even numbers B8-16 seem tough, some of the spots are so small you probably couldn’t even fit a 5 person tent. Short walk to the beach, views were AMAZING!! Check the tides for good tidepools! You can walk to the “downtown” area but we drove. Clean bathrooms! We booked online the night before and I’m glad we did because when we got there, all of the sites were reserved.

reviews.author: K S
reviews.text:
Our favorite campground!

This is all because of the amazing park hosts and volunteer hosts! The facilities are very clean, the restrooms especially are amongst the cleanest I have stayed in. The hosts are the nicest, and keep the area super clean. We were amazed at how diligently each site is cleaned after, they do an amazing job setting up each camper for success. They also have firewood and fire starters available which made the whole trip that much better.

We loved our first stay so much we booked three more trips immediately, thank you for giving us something to look forward to, especially during these times.

reviews.author: Marnie Ravitch
reviews.text:
Someone recommended we stay here on our trip up the west coast. We booked two nights last minute.  I really wish we could spend more time here.  If you love the ocean and beaches as well as huge, lush, shaded camping sites, this is for you!  A state park with fill rv hookups is kind of unusual. The place is spotless.  The adjacent park area is breathtaking. I can't wait to come back and spend more time!

We had to come in at night. I don't recommend that unless you're very comfortable parking in the dark.  It's very dark here at night.

Staff is remarkably helpful.

We didn't use the restrooms so I can't speak to that.

Our site was practically level; took very little tinkering.  Utilities in great shape, well maintained. Plenty of sky for our starlink.  I think t mobile worked fine here, too. Very spacious and private sites. Plenty of space for chairs, etc.

Not far from Crescent City but a much better campground than you will find there.

The two nights we were here, we only heard the ocean. No loud neighbors or traffic whatsoever.

The picture attached was taken from the edge of our site.

We really can't wait to come back!!

reviews.author: Jenny Alexander
reviews.text:
Harris Beach Campground State Park is well—maintained and attractive. We were in site 6A, which had a large grassy area and vegetation separating the sites on either side of us. A lot of the sites were under trees, which would be great on a hot day, but it was raining so we it wasn’t as dark and gloomy in our site.
It cleared enough for a walk down to the day use area and a spectacular sunset

reviews.author: Amber
reviews.text: This palace is a one stop delight. Offering much to be desired. Ranger Danae is very openly to changes in schedule causi g need for reimbursement... this truly made our day. Stop in here. Make reservation. Support local. And Enjoy your time.. BIG thanks 😊 to these awesome caretakers. Try the yurt... they come heated.

reviews.author: Tin Tumbleweed
reviews.text:
Verizon speeds of 20 Mbps download and 4 Mbps upload with a roof mounted Pepwave antenna. It suffered from substantial congestion during peak hours. Starlink was 100/10 with residential. AT&T was 191/45 via phone.

This was among the best maintained state parks we've been to. Pristine roads and asphalt site pads. Very clean with no trash. The site was slightly unlevel side to side. Site A20 has a spectacular ocean view. The sites are very large and are separated from others with dense hedges.

The checkin time of 4pm and some road/construction noise were really the only negatives.

reviews.author: camp-roadtripper4795262
reviews.text: We stayed here for four days with full hookups. The place is kept very clean. The camp host take pride in their campground, will definitely stay again.

reviews.author: camp-uallanman
reviews.text: The ranger at check in was very friendly and helpful. Our site was clean even tho we checked in a bit early. Love the different beach access points. Close to town and other scenic points along Rt. 101. We were in a 35’ Class A, towing. Full hookups.

reviews.author: camp-heyitsjustme
reviews.text: Nice hike to cool little beach. Clean bathrooms and shower. 4 bars Verizon. Our particular site was filled with dog doodoo. Must have had folks from Eureka there before us

reviews.author: Phil-R.
reviews.text: We pulled in on a whim and geez this place is nice. Nice little access to the beach you can drive to. Really a cool beach. Campground is so nice! Full hookups.

reviews.author: rls1936
reviews.text:
Overall, a wonderful place. Easy access from Hwy 101, just north of Brookings. Easy drive by at ranger kiosk for check-in. Our full hookup site was functional. You could just see the ocean through the trees from our site. This is the best Oregon State Park we have been to (our 9th). Bathrooms were the same as all the other Oregon state parks, adequate. Our site was easily long enough for a 40' RV and vehicle, look at the site lengths on the website, some are short. No road noise at our site. Our site was very level. Walking around the campground, I would avoid the sites closest to Hwy 101 due to road noise and being un-level.

The location is great, it is about 35 minutes to the Redwood parks. Lots of hiking, Samuel Boardman SP to the north, Oregon redwoods trail and all the redwoods to the south.

AT&T cell service was excellent, all the bars of 4G. No problem streaming from phones without boosting. Many HDTV channels were available.

reviews.author: TedandKierstan
reviews.text:
Popular campground in a beautiful setting. Amazing beach and lots of trees.

Clean and well cared for State Park. We will be back.

CG Fee + $8 reservation service.

With our upgraded tech we were able to work remotely without any problems.

Enjoyed mornings on the beach and evening sunsets.

Make your reservations in advance if you want to get a spot.

Campsites are a little tight but doable but check the campsite details closely when making your reservation.

There is a little road noise from HWY 101 for the campsites in the back row.

reviews.author: camp-meah1
reviews.text:
[Internet. Verizon via iPhone 12: 12 mbps down and 10 mbps up with 31 ms ping.]

I understand now why this campground is coveted! I’d give this place 6-stars if I could.

The many, many positives

→ It’s super, duper clean.

→ The roads and campsites are black-top paved.

→The bathrooms and showers are not only clean but pretty!

→ The showers are divine. The showers are free! (I just got here from CA campgrounds where all showers are pay showers.) The water is ALWAYS hot. The water pressure is insane. You never have an “oh, someone must be flushing a toilet” moment. The shower rooms aren’t cold!

→ There’s a dump station with water fill that’s free.

→ The campsites are pretty private.

→ Our campsite had water and power. What a luxury.

→ The proximity to the beach which is gorgeous!

The one negative

→ It’s such a great campground that it books up quick. We only stayed one night.

5-stars - This campground is just perfect.

reviews.author: camp-lgbounsall
reviews.text:
We've stayed at Harris Beach State Park before, and both times we've enjoyed our stay immensely. The park is extremely well maintained, most sites have plenty of space, not all have full h/u.

PROS

Many sunny sites with good elbow room (some sites are closer than others)

Our site had nice vegetation to divide each camp site

Lawn near each site

Trash and Grey water cisterns near each campsite

Several shower/bath rooms

Free hot showers

Clean showers and bathroom

Kids play structure

Fire rings/pits

$5 firewood bundles for sale from 3-6pm

Quiet

Short walk to the beach and sunsets

Tide pools

Level paved sites with accessible picnic tables

Close to town for groceries/restaurants/shopping

Quiet

Not too crowded during winter

Some sites have a 'peek-a-boo' ocean view. Our site did (A33)

CONS

No Wifi (if that's your thing)

ATT had 2 bars

Not all sites have full hook-ups some have just water and power (but grey water cisterns are very close to each site)

The best beach front sites are hard to get.

Sites closer to Highway 101 have road noise

Overall we love Harris Beach State Park for all of the PROS and none of the cons would deter us in the least from staying here. The views throughout the park are wonderful, nice paved areas to walk your dog(s), easy walk down to the day-use area or drive if you have limited mobility. Path from the day-use to the beach is nice.

reviews.author: Paige16
reviews.text:
pros: clean bathrooms & showers, water spigots nearby, can walk down to the beach & there are amazing sunset views, decent sized sites, convenient location to state scenic corridor

cons: campsites are pretty close together & it was packed on the weekend

reviews.author: redfox
reviews.text: We did a 18 days road trip, this campground was one of our stop and so far it was the best one. We got everything! The forest right next to the beach, it’s a quite place, very clean bathrooms, the energy, it’s truly AMAZING. I’ll love to go back ASAP

reviews.author: Kiangsy
reviews.text:
Brookings is a "banana belt" zone so while the wind is blustery and chilly, you get a lot fewer foggy days than other places along this beautiful coast. And in Brookings the very best place you can stay is at Harris Beach SP. We've stayed at other places here so I speak from experience!

While only a few sites have actual water views, all are good size, level, asphalt pads with green grass and lots of lush bushes and tall trees. We stayed in the 50 amp FHU section and even our satellite connected although we were surrounded by beautiful forest. Picnic table and fire pit with grill with good space to spread out. Easy access from Hwy 101 with good signage and decent interior roads. Unhook your toad at the campground kiosk area. On-site rangers and volunteers keep this park pristine, are super friendly, and have a lot of good info about the area.

The route down to the beach is very steep and there are a couple nice, easy trails along the top with outstanding views of Harris Beach. Plenty of parking at the beach level with clean restrooms and interpretive signs.

Nice playground for the kiddos. Firewood sold in the park. A park with something for everyone.
